newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Granada and YTTV agree on price.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Granada and YTTV agree on price.

text.p: Granada Group Plc, negotiating to take over Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Plc, has agreed a price of 1175p/share with the Yorkshire board, Granada chairman Gerry Robinson said on Wednesday.
"We have agreed a price in outline of 11.75 pounds," Robinson told Reuters in a telephone interview. "The boards of the two companies have agreed on the price."
The two companies announced on Monday that they were in "preliminary discussions" for Granada to acquire the 73 percent of Yorkshire it does not own at 1175p/share.
The deal values Yorkshire at a total of 710-720 million stg, including warrants.

Robinson said the deal would benefit Granada in two ways. Firstly, it would allow Granada to boost its position as a broadcaster in northern England and sell the north to advertisers as a single region and secondly, it would strengthen Granada's programme production.
The deal would require regulatory approval and Robinson said he believed it would still take some two months to complete even if everything went smoothly.
Robinson said Granada would not need to sell its 10.8 percent stake in BSkyB Plc to fund the move for Yorkshire. The BSkyB stake is worth over one billion stg.
Looking at Granada's first half results, Robinson said the company had met the promises it made during its 3.9 billion stg takeover of Forte in January 1996.
"Everything that was promised has been delivered - and a bit more. The disposal programme has delivered all the cash but from fewer asset sales," he said.
Granada this week took proceeds from post-Forte disposals to over 1.3 billion stg when it sold Brown's hotel in London.

It has a further eight so-called "Exclusive" luxury hotels on the market. Robinson said Granada was in negotiations over a number of these properties but did not rule out ultimately retaining one or two.
He said the sale of the company's 68 percent stake in the Savoy Hotel Plc was now on the agenda.
"We're confident we'll find a sensible way for Granada to exit that and meanwhile the Savoy's profitability is rising sharply," he said.
